model: Two-stream optics of a non-absorbing deck: the base returns R = tau*/(1+tau*) of the light below it and T = 1/(1+tau*) of the light above it, with tau* = tau(1-g). The light above is the solar beam, reddened by its path to the deck's altitude and by ozone's Chappuis band at its measured peak, plus the diffuse sky over the deck; the sun is taken at its refracted elevation (Bennett 1982). The diffuse sky is the bake's own multiple-scattering solution, every order the transport resolves, not a first-order approximation: that shelf is the light that survives after the sun has set on the ground and on the deck, so the base keeps brightening through twilight while the beam is already gone. The light below is the sky the deck lets through to the ground it shades, reflected by a Lambertian surface of the albedo below and re-reflected between that surface and the base (1/(1 - albedo*R)). Every flux is the bake's own spectral transport, per sun step; no coefficient is fitted to a colour. Written as linear sRGB, normalised against the highest sun, on a grid of one row per second of the day: the deck's optics are re-solved at each row's own elevation, while the sky's diffuse irradiance and the beam's tint are carried over from the 360-step dome grid, which is the only part of this that needs the transport.
